# MuTracer

> MuTracer is a progressive, physically based path tracer for the browser. npm package `@meimu/mutracer`. WebGPU with a WebGL 2 fallback, OpenPBR 1.1 materials, TinyBVH (WebAssembly) acceleration, and denoising with a built-in JNLM filter or Intel Open Image Denoise (OIDN). MIT licensed.

## Usage essentials

- Install: `npm install @meimu/mutracer` (+ `three` for the Three.js helpers). ESM with TypeScript declarations; every option has TSDoc with its default.
- A scene is a plain object `{ meshes: Mesh[], lights: SceneLight[], background? }`. A `Mesh(geometry, material)` is placed with `mesh.matrixWorld` (column-major mat4, gl-matrix compatible).
- `const renderer = new Renderer({ canvas }); renderer.setSize(w, h);` then call `renderer.render(scene, camera)` once per `requestAnimationFrame`. It accumulates samples up to `renderer.maxSamples` (default 2048) and returns a status.
- Statuses: PREPARING (6, device init / BVH build), COMPILING_SHADER (1), RENDERING (2), DENOISING (3), FINISHED (4), ERROR (5). Keep calling `render()` through PREPARING and COMPILING_SHADER.
- Scene membership, mesh matrix elements, geometry/material references, light parameters and background values are detected automatically on each render. After material parameter edits call `material.markUpdated()`; after geometry attribute edits call `geometry.markUpdated()`; after texture pixel or UV-array element edits call `texture.markUpdated()`. Camera and renderer options are checked every frame. Both WebGPU and WebGL 2 refit transform-only changes. Stable geometry arrays with a new version update only affected vertex/BLAS regions; replaced arrays, displacement and simplification require full preparation. `geometry.dynamic` defaults to false; true selects built-in bvh2 and rebuilds when total node surface area exceeds twice the last build.
- Three.js: `const sync = new THREESceneSync(threeScene);` then `sync.update(); renderer.render(sync.scene, fromTHREECamera(threeCamera));` each frame. `sync.dispose()` releases conversion caches. Three.js attribute/index edits require `needsUpdate = true`; texture pixel edits require `texture.needsUpdate = true`. CPU skinning and morph targets own per-source-mesh dynamic geometry and skip unchanged poses. InstancedMesh expands count into shared-geometry meshes, retains its prefix on count edits, and caches material variants by source material and instance RGB (unlit colors also multiply emissionColor). Instance matrix/color array edits require the corresponding attribute.needsUpdate = true. Distinct colors grow material count; cached variants live until dispose. BatchedMesh, instanced morphTexture and skinned instancing warn once and convert as ordinary meshes. Supports MeshStandardMaterial / MeshPhysicalMaterial / MeshBasicMaterial; directional, point, spot, rect-area and ambient lights; `scene.environment` as an equirectangular float DataTexture. Prefer Three.js `GLTFLoader` + `THREESceneSync` over the built-in `loadGLTF`.
- Materials: `OpenPBRMaterial` with OpenPBR names (`baseColor`, `baseMetalness`, `specularRoughness`, `specularIor`, `transmissionWeight`, `coatWeight`, `subsurfaceWeight`, `fuzzWeight`, `thinFilmWeight`, `emissionLuminance`, ...). Colors are linear RGB; 8-bit textures are sRGB.
- Lights: `RectLight(size, color, intensity)` emits along its local -Z; `SphereLight(position, color, intensity, radius)`; `SpotLight(position, direction, color, intensity, radius, innerDeg, outerDeg)`; `DirectionalLight(position, color, intensity)` shines from `position` toward the origin; `EnvironmentLight(texture)` for equirectangular HDR (`await loadRGBE(url)`).
- Backgrounds: omit to show the environment; `[r, g, b, a]` linear color (`[0,0,0,0]` = transparent canvas, pair with `material.shadowCatcher = true`); a `Texture`; or `{ type: 'GroundedSkybox', map, height, radius }`.
- Sampling: `renderer.samplingPattern = 'sobol' | 'zsobol' | 'random'`; default `'sobol'`. Choose `'zsobol'` explicitly for low spp without a denoiser. OIDN never changes the pattern. See `docs/sampling.md` for the progressive budget caveat.
- Denoising: `await renderer.setDenoiser()` attaches the built-in JNLM filter (WebGPU and WebGL 2, no download, about 17 ms at 1080p; `strength?`, default 1). `await renderer.setDenoiser({ type: 'oidn', model: 'standard' | 'small' | 'cleanAuxLarge', weightsBaseUrl?, whileConverging? })` uses OIDN (WebGPU only), which is cleaner at 1–2 spp; `model` or `weightsBaseUrl` alone also selects OIDN. Standard/small weights load from bundled assets; large networks use `oidn-weights@2.3.0-1` on jsDelivr. Vite development needs `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['@meimu/mutracer']` for weight and optional wasm asset URLs. Self-host all networks from `node_modules/oidn-weights/` with `weightsBaseUrl`.
- Final stills: `await renderer.renderOfflineFrame(scene, camera, { samples })`, then `renderer.prepareForExport()` and `canvas.toBlob(...)`. Linear HDR pixels: `await renderer.getRawOutput()`.
- BVHs build automatically inside `render()` with the built-in JavaScript builder (a port of TinyBVH's binned SAH builder). `renderer.bvhBuilder = 'tinybvh'` uses the TinyBVH WebAssembly module instead, loaded on demand and built before the first frame (`await renderer.prepareScene(scene)` builds up front); `renderer.bvhSpatialSplits = true` enables its slower SBVH build.

## Three.js render loop

Create one `THREESceneSync` after building or loading `threeScene`. Update it
before each render so scene edits are reflected while unchanged resources are
reused. Convert the camera each frame:

```ts
import { Renderer, THREESceneSync, fromTHREECamera } from '@meimu/mutracer';

const renderer = new Renderer({ canvas });
const sync = new THREESceneSync(threeScene);

function frame() {
  sync.update();
  renderer.render(sync.scene, fromTHREECamera(threeCamera));
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
frame();
```

Call `sync.dispose()` when finished to release conversion caches and
`renderer.dispose()` to release GPU resources. `fromTHREEScene(threeScene)`
remains available for one-shot conversion; every call creates fresh objects.

## Common pitfalls

- Material parameter, geometry attribute or texture pixel edits require the edited object’s `markUpdated()`. Mesh transforms and scene membership changes need no extra call.
- `createPlaneGeometry()` is 2×2 in XZ; `createSphereGeometry()` and `createCubeGeometry()` span -1..1. Scale with `matrixWorld`.
- Rect lights are one-sided; rotate them to face the scene.
- OIDN denoising, auto exposure and HDR output require WebGPU; WebGL 2 denoises with JNLM only.
- Call `renderer.setSize` with drawing-buffer pixels and update `camera.aspect` on resize.
